observation.description: @expo/snapback-react 0.1.7 exposes no offline surface at all: the exported hooks/observers (useSnapbackQuery/Queries/Mutation/Connection/Presence, observeSnapbackQueries/Presence) carry rows, status, and the connection axis, but no freshness ('retained' vs 'current'), no retention fact, and no outbox/queued-mutation state — grep of the packaged index.mjs finds zero occurrences of freshness/retention/outbox/queued. A React field-notebook cannot render the documented honest freshness state or a queued-changes badge from the first-party arm; this arm's shell wires the freshness-state chip to connection status with a finding comment. The headless client carries all of these facts (handle.freshness, handle.retention, rqsStoreInfo, replayQueuedMutations, outboxDiagnostics), so the projection is missing, not the substrate.
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a1-snapback-web/evidence/phase-cold.json (the handle-level facts the hooks do not project)

competitorOutcome.description: Firebase exposes SnapshotMetadata.fromCache on every snapshot, so a React view renders cache-vs-server honestly with no extra machinery; the frozen Firebase arm surfaced it. InstantDB's React hooks return offline-first state transparently.

mustNotRegress: The connection axis honesty already surfaced by useSnapbackConnection, and the headless handle facts the projection would ride.
smallestCoherentFix: Project freshness/retention onto the query hook result (per-query) and add an outbox hook (queued count + replay state) over the existing client facts, with a packaged-closure test that cold-boots a provider offline and reads freshness:'retained' from the hook.
acceptanceWitness: A React component renders 'Retained' from useSnapbackQuery's own result during an offline cold boot and a queued-changes count after an offline mutation, on the public closure.
